# temps_ingress_connector (Resource)

Publishes apps through an outbound tunnel (for example a Cloudflare Tunnel) running on chosen nodes, for hosts that cannot accept inbound connections.

Import with `<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_ingress_connector" "tunnel" {
  name          = "edge-tunnel"
  provider_type = "cloudflare"
  node_ids      = [2, 3]
  host_suffix   = "apps.example.com"
  values        = jsonencode({ account_id = var.cloudflare_account_id })
  secrets       = { api_token = var.cloudflare_tunnel_token }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the connector.
- `node_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the nodes that run the tunnel. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `provider_type` (String) Tunnel provider, for example `cloudflare`.

### Optional

- `auto_publish` (Boolean) Publish every app's hostnames automatically.
- `host_suffix` (String) Suffix of the hostnames it publishes.
- `secrets` (Map of String, Sensitive) Provider credentials. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `values` (String) Provider settings, for example the account ID. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.

### Read-Only

- `domain` (String) Domain the connector publishes under.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<id>`.
- `last_error` (String) Last error.
- `status` (String) Connector status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id>
terraform import temps_ingress_connector.tunnel 9
```
